Explain how a VPN works in simple words
7:09 PM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet. Everything you send goes through that tunnel scrambled, so nobody in between can read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device scrambles your traffic before it leaves.
The scrambled traffic travels to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unscrambles it and sends it to the website for you.
The website sees the VPN's address instead of yours.

This helps on public Wi-Fi, because strangers on the same network can't read what you send. It also hides your location from websites. It does not make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
